summary: The decoded operands are now receipt-backed (CheckRun aa600f3fb29146a99e15abbec79139fd: completed, tests_passed, exit 0, 22 parsed observations, 0 parse errors) and they name the committed history exactly: index 2 is a ConfChangeV2 with transition JointImplicit that removes node 4 - a change that alters no voter set, since node 4 is not a member - index 3 is a normal entry, and index 4 is a ConfChangeV2 with transition JointImplicit that adds node 4, with no leave-joint entry anywhere in the applied range. Nodes 3, 1 and 4 apply that history in order (indices 18-20) and reject the second change with 'config is already joint', while index 21 keeps the counters and violations=0 and index 16 repeats the deterministic guard case. The account of why the required leave is missing is now specific and source-grounded: appliedTo proposes the zero-change leave only when the node applying the joint change is the leader, so a joint change whose proposer is displaced before it applies its own change leaves the cluster joint with nobody having proposed the leave, and the next leader then sees a non-joint tracker plus a pendingConfIndex predating the committed change - exactly the state the deterministic case shows the guard admitting. So the asserted availability defect now rests on three receipts: the guard admission under stale leader-local state, the actual changes in the committed history, and the in-order application that reaches the rejection. I promoted the decoded history as behaviour knowledge and kept scope and counterweights explicit: the receipt shows which changes are in the log but not which node proposed each entry or whether that proposer was displaced before applying it, so the reason no leave was appended is still an inference from the appliedTo condition plus the decoded changes; the history is one seed and one log position; violations=0 keeps the claim about availability rather than safety; the target's Config comment documents the checks as best-effort with false negatives, so what the receipts add is that the consequence is a panic the applying node cannot avoid while following its duty; and the election-to-stale-state path remains source-argued, the decoded range is capped at eight entries, the harness recovers the panic, and storage faults, other cluster sizes and a rejecting leader are still outside the event set.
